APH's 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 shows Communications Solutions at ~62% of net sales growing 85% in USD and 42% ORGANICALLY y/y, attributed to outsized organic growth in IT datacom with particular strength in AI-related. That kills my rank-5 premise outright: 'lowest AI torque per dollar in the cluster' is not merely unevidenced, it is contradicted. I am moving APH from rank 5 to rank 4, above MRVL. I am NOT moving it above ALAB, and I want to be precise about why: 62% is Communications Solutions, which also contains mobile networks and broadband, and a stand-alone IT-datacom share of total sales is still not established -- so APH's AI torque is materially higher than I credited but is not demonstrated to exceed a pure-play scale-up name that guided ~30% above consensus. Two things now cut the other way and I am carrying them as case_against rather than netting them out: 85% USD against 42% organic means roughly half the segment's growth is the CommScope Connectivity and Cable Solutions acquisition (closed 2026-01-09), not underlying demand; and that deal was funded by term loans, so APH has added leverage to buy the fiber-optic interconnect content that partly explains its own AI exposure. Separately I accept your strengthening->intact downgrade and note the resulting tension rather than hiding it: I am PROMOTING a name on the same day thesis DOWNGRADES it. Both are defensible because we are answering different questions -- your downgrade is about the quality of the evidence in the thesis record, my promotion is about relative position within the cluster on a primary-source segment disclosure that post-dates your evidence. If you want to re-verify, the 10-Q segment table is the document.

answers_to_your_questions.answer: Primary source, APH 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 (filed 2026-07-31, accn 0001104659-26-089194). The Communications Solutions segment is approximately 62% of Q2-2026 net sales (60% for the first six months) and its net sales rose 85% in USD, 84% in constant currency and 42% ORGANICALLY versus Q2-2025; the filing attributes the increase to 'outsized organic growth in the IT datacom market, with particular strength in AI-related' demand. Separately, APH closed the acquisition of CommScope's Connectivity and Cable Solutions business on 2026-01-09 (adds fiber-optic interconnect for IT datacom and communications networks), funded with Delayed Draw Term Loans ($1,534.1M drawn under each; the 364-day loan stood at $934.1M at 06-30 after a $600M repayment). NOT established: a stand-alone IT-datacom share of total net sales -- the sentences retrieved give the segment share (62%) and the segment growth, not the market split. Two facts follow: (1) the 'lowest AI torque per dollar in the cluster' premise for APH is contradicted by its own largest segment growing 42% organically on AI-related datacom demand; (2) APH now carries acquisition leverage and fiber content that the ladder did not model.
